title: lessons.jsonl reading in B4 is unbounded — no limit, no pruning, token consumption grows with every improve step
description: The cron prompt's STEP 5 IMPROVE STEP instructs: '(a) read ~/gig/lessons.jsonl + ~/gig/applied.jsonl stats'. There is no LIMIT N on how many rows are read. lessons.jsonl grows one row per observed outcome event. With hourly passes, up to 5 applications per pass, and some fraction generating outcomes, the file can accumulate thousands of rows over weeks. At 4-pass cadence for improve, every ~4 hours the LLM reads the ENTIRE lessons.jsonl into context. At several hundred tokens per JSON row, a month of operation could push lessons.jsonl to 50k+ tokens per improve read, approaching context window limits. The spec at line 63 says 'Read ~/gig/lessons.jsonl (all rows)' with no qualification. No pruning, rotation, or limit is specified anywhere. There is no test that the file is bounded.

additionalEvidence.note: Cron prompt: '(a) read ~/gig/lessons.jsonl + ~/gig/applied.jsonl stats → compute per-category accept_rate' — no limit specified

fix: Add to the improve step prompt: 'Read only the last 50 rows of ~/gig/lessons.jsonl (use tail -n 50) for the improve computation. Older rows are already encoded in the current strategy.json from prior improve runs.' Alternatively, archive lessons.jsonl > N rows to lessons-archive.jsonl and only keep the recent N. Specify a lessons.jsonl row cap in the spec and test that the improve step uses tail or limit.
